bayesEfron: Fully Bayesian Deconvolution with Efron's Log-Spline Prior

Source: R/bayesEfron-package.R
bayesEfron-package.Rd

Estimates the distribution of true effects from a set of estimates with known standard errors, as in a meta-analysis or a multisite trial, using the fully Bayesian version of Efron's log-spline prior described in Lee and Sui (2025) doi:10.3390/math13162639 . The fit returns posterior draws of the distribution of effects, from which the summaries of each effect are computed. The package also provides sampler and grid diagnostics, plots made with 'ggplot2', and model comparison by approximate leave-one-out cross-validation. The estimated distribution can be passed to the 'ebnm' package for comparison with empirical Bayes estimates. The model is written in 'Stan' and is fitted with 'CmdStan' through the 'cmdstanr' package.

Details

To get started, read vignette("bayesEfron"), which walks through a complete analysis of the callback gaps of 97 firms. The model, its prior distributions and the way it is fitted are described in bayes_efron_fit().

Functions

  • as_bef_data() extracts the estimates and their standard errors from a list, a data frame or a metafor::escalc() object and checks them.

  • make_efron_grid() builds the grid and the spline basis, and plot() shows them together with the estimates.

  • bayes_efron_fit() fits the model and returns a bef_fit object, which has summary(), coef(), confint() and other methods.

  • diagnose() returns sampler and grid diagnostics.

  • g_summary() summarizes the estimated distribution of effects, and site_summary() and exceedance_prob() summarize the site effects.

  • plot() plots a fit. The functions that it calls can also be called directly: plot_g(), plot_sites(), plot_shrinkage(), plot_exceedance(), plot_site_posterior(), plot_diagnostics(), plot_loo(), plot_ppc(), plot_mcmc() and, for simulated data, plot_recovery().

  • predict() returns draws of the effect or of the estimate of a new site.

  • loo() estimates how well a fit predicts the estimate of a site that is left out, and compare_efron_grids() compares fits on several grids by that measure.

  • as_normalmix() returns the estimate of \(g\) as a normalmix object for the ebnm package.

  • bayes_efron_compile() compiles the two Stan programs before the first fit, and bayes_efron_clear_cache() deletes the compiled models.

Data sets and vignettes

The following data sets come with a stored fit, which can be used without CmdStan.

  • krw_discrimination and krw_fit: the callback gaps of 97 firms, analyzed in vignette("bayesEfron").

  • raudenbush1985 and raudenbush_fit: a meta-analysis of 19 studies, analyzed in vignette("teacher-expectancy").

  • twin_towers and twin_towers_fit: a simulated data set with known true effects, analyzed in vignette("twin-towers").

The data set star_schools contains estimates of the effect of small classes in kindergarten in 79 schools of Project STAR, a multisite trial.

The other vignettes cover data input, the choice of the grid, diagnostics, plots, a comparison with empirical Bayes methods, the model, and the implementation. browseVignettes("bayesEfron") lists them all.
